name: @w6w-apps/vapi
description: Place and manage voice AI phone calls, and read the assistant, phone number, squad, tool and file catalogs behind them, on Vapi.

w6w.longDescription:
Vapi is voice-AI infrastructure: assistants (a transcriber + LLM + voice pipeline) are configured once in the Vapi dashboard or API, then driven over phone or web calls. The unit this app moves around is the call — created against an existing Assistant, Squad or Workflow, plus the catalogs (assistants, phone numbers, squads, tools, files) a workflow needs to pick from before placing one.

This app deliberately does not create or update Assistants, Squads or Tools: each is a deeply nested, polymorphic configuration object (a transcriber, a model, a voice provider, a compliance plan, and — for Tools — one of twelve unrelated shapes from a plain webhook to a Bash sandbox), the kind of object meant to be authored once in the dashboard and then referenced by id, not re-typed into a workflow form. What the app does cover in full is the operational surface: start a call against any of those, list and inspect calls, rename or delete a call's stored data, and read every catalog by id.

Health checks track Vapi's own status page (a genuine Better Stack page at status.vapi.ai, not the Statuspage-shaped decoy at vapi.statuspage.io) alongside the derived credential-liveness check; there is no documented usage/quota endpoint or rate-limit header on this API, so quota is declared unavailable rather than guessed.
